parts.label: a
parts.technique: Simple harmonic motion - maximum speed from period and amplitude
parts.reason: SHM is not mentioned anywhere in the statements; no statement covers oscillatory motion, angular frequency, or v=aω relations. This topic is entirely absent from the specification list.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Simple harmonic motion - time from O to a given displacement using x=asin(ωt)
parts.reason: Same SHM topic as (a); SHM is not a listed statement anywhere in the specification, so this part is out regardless of the underlying trig manipulation.

parts.label: main
parts.technique: Circular motion of a particle on the inside of a smooth hemispherical bowl (conical pendulum type problem), resolving forces and using v=rω / centripetal acceleration
parts.reason: Circular motion (horizontal circles, conical pendulum, centripetal force) is not mentioned in any Mechanics statement (M6-M9 only cover quantities/units, kinematics in a straight line and projectiles, Newton's laws/friction, and moments). No statement provides for resolving forces on a particle moving in a horizontal circle.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Variable acceleration kinematics using a = v(dv/dx) (chain rule for acceleration as function of displacement)
parts.reason: M7.4 only lists a = dv/dt = d^2r/dt^2 and v,r as integrals/derivatives with respect to t; it does not include the a = v dv/dx form derived via the chain rule with respect to x. P7.4 covers connected rates of change generally, but the specific technique of finding acceleration from v(x) via v dv/dx applied in a kinematics deceleration context is not stated at this depth, and no alternative in-spec method reaching full marks is offered by the mark scheme (only this chain-rule route is given).

parts.technique: Centre of mass of a solid hemisphere by integration

parts.technique: Centre of mass of composite solid (hemisphere+cone) and equilibrium/toppling condition

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Circular motion on a string in a vertical circle - tension as function of angle using Newton's second law along the radius plus energy equation
parts.reason: Vertical circular motion, tension varying with angle, and centripetal acceleration v^2/a are not covered by any Mechanics statement; circular motion (horizontal or vertical) does not appear anywhere in M6-M9.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Finding speed when string becomes slack (tension=0) in vertical circular motion
parts.reason: Continuation of the vertical circular motion problem; circular motion is not in the specification statements, and this part also depends on the out-of-spec result from (a).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Projectile motion after string goes slack, finding maximum height using resolved components of velocity and constant acceleration under gravity
parts.reason: Although projectile motion under gravity (M7.5) is itself in spec, this part depends entirely on the out-of-spec circular motion results (the speed and angle from (a)/(b)) with no independent in-spec route to those values, so the part as a whole cannot be credited as in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Hooke's Law to find modulus of elasticity of a second elastic string from equilibrium of two strings
parts.reason: Hooke's Law and elastic strings/modulus of elasticity are not present in any statement (M6-M9 do not mention elasticity).

parts.label: b

parts.reason: Requires both Hooke's Law (elastic strings) and SHM, neither of which appears in any statement.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Using SHM formula v²=ω²(a²-x²) to find speed when a string becomes slack
parts.reason: SHM is not covered by any statement, and this part depends on the out-of-spec SHM setup from (b).

parts.reason: SHM is entirely absent from the specification statements; this part is a direct continuation of the out-of-spec SHM analysis.
